question: In the spent FCC catalyst recovery route, what is the second-largest contributor to the wet-recovery stage's climate-change impact, what share does it have, and in which unit operation is it used?
expect: the 350 kg sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) input, 29.2%; alkaline roasting (sec. 3.1.1; Table 1)
rendered:
Based on the documents provided, I found the answer in the first document, specifically on page 7, in the section "3.1.1. Environmental Impacts of the Wet Recovery Stage."

The second-largest contributor to the wet-recovery stage's climate-change impact is sodium carbonate (Na2CO3). It accounts for 29.2% of the climate-change impact, and it is used in the alkaline roasting unit operation.

The climate-change impact of the wet-recovery stage is 1,536.56 kg CO2-eq per t of spent catalyst, and sodium carbonate contributes 448.20 kg CO2-eq to this impact.
